# Mercury — calculated thermodynamic functions

<!-- generated-by: sync-thermochemistry.mjs -->

Source: SRC-000469, NIST Chemistry WebBook / Chase (1998), retrieved 2026-10-05. These are calculations from dated fits, not new measurements. Values below are rounded to four decimal places for computational comparison; this is not a statement of physical precision. Uncertainty: UNKNOWN. Basis: **mol Hg**.

[Full calculation and limits](../0080-Mercury-Hg-Thermochemistry.md) · [Complete 101-point-per-fit CSV](0080-Mercury-Hg-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.csv) · [Exact coefficients](../data/structured/0080-Mercury-Hg-NIST-Thermochemistry.yaml)

| Fit | Variant | T / K | Cp° / J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | S° / J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | H°(T)−H°(298.15 K) / kJ mol⁻¹ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GAS:01 | UNSPECIFIED-IN-FIT-TABLE | 629.8390 | 20.7739 | 190.5121 | 6.8905 |
| GAS:01 | UNSPECIFIED-IN-FIT-TABLE | 3314.9195 | 20.7714 | 225.0363 | 62.7083 |
| GAS:01 | UNSPECIFIED-IN-FIT-TABLE | 6000.0000 | 21.1426 | 237.4130 | 118.7624 |

Each row uses only the named phase and fit interval. Do not subtract rows from different phases to obtain transition enthalpy without first resolving their standard-state reference offsets.
